Indiana: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Indiana on the map

Key dates

  • Voter registration deadline (online, in person, or by mail postmarked): October 5, 2026. You can register or check your registration at indianavoters.in.gov.
  • Early in-person (absentee) voting: October 6, 2026 to November 2, 2026. Early voting ends at noon on November 2. Locations and hours depend on your county.
  • Last day for the county to receive a mail absentee ballot application: October 22, 2026. Indiana requires an approved reason to vote by mail. Completed mail ballots must arrive by 6 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. local time.

Official election information: vote.gov

Ballot measures

Public Question #1: Bail (Article 1, Section 17)

This constitutional amendment would let courts deny bail to a person charged with an offense other than murder or treason if the proof is evident or the presumption strong, and the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community.

Yes: A yes vote amends the constitution so courts can deny bail in more cases, beyond murder and treason, when both conditions are met.
No: A no vote keeps the current rule, under which bail may be denied only for murder or treason when the proof is evident or the presumption strong.

Public Question #2: Residency of City and Town Court Judges (Article 6, Section 6)

This constitutional amendment would let a city or town court judge live in the county where the court is located, or in the bordering county closest to the city or town, instead of having to live in the city or town itself.

Yes: A yes vote amends the constitution so city and town court judges may live in the court's county or in the nearest bordering county.
No: A no vote keeps the current requirement that city and town court judges live in the city or town where they serve.
